newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open steady, market awaits PPI data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open steady, market awaits PPI data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury securities prices opened steady with a slightly positive bias on Friday as market participants awaited release of the Producer Price Index for June.

The Labor Department was to release the data at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast, on average, an unchanged reading. Analysts expect the figures to serve as further confirmation of contained inflation. A change of more than 0.1 percent, up or down, would be a surprise, they said.
No other data are due for release today.

"It's most likely to be continuation of the range we've been in since Monday," said Patrick Dimick, trader at UBS Securities Inc. "If PPI is super friendly, we could break out some to the upside. But this is not the number that's going to generate a lot of follow-up buying or selling."
That type of number will come Tuesday, when June retail sales are scheduled for release.

Dimick said the September futures contract has been trading in a range of 113-12 to 114-03 recently, and a minor breakout to the upside is possible on a tame PPI reading. But he does not expect any dramatic change in the contract.
Economists pointed out that there has been disinflation thus far this year in the PPI -- all the more reason to expect a tame reading.

Producer price data are looked at for signs of incipient inflationary pressures that will eventually force manufacturers to pass on price increases to consumers. However, much of this recovery has been characterized by the inability of producers to pass along price increases. Instead, they have had to cut costs and profit margins.
Thus the number has lost some of the clout it once had.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was trading up 5/32 at 100-30/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
At the short end, three-month bills were down one basis point at 5.02 percent and six-month bills were up one basis point at 5.11 percent. Year bills were down one basis point at 5.22 percent.
Ten-year issues were up 4/32 at 102-26/32, yielding 6.24 percent. Five years were up 3/32 at 100-17/32 to yield 6.12 percent. Two-year notes were up 1/32 at 100-7/32 to yield 5.88 percent.
